newsletters.title: Liguria
newsletters.subtitle: The Vertical Riviera
newsletters.shortDescription: Two coasts compared: the Levante premium against the Ponente value.
newsletters.description: Italy's narrowest region is a 350-kilometre crescent pressed between the Maritime Alps and the sea — and its two coasts could hardly be more different. East of Genoa, the Levante trades in postcards: Portofino, the Cinque Terre, and prices to match. West, the Ponente unfurls toward France through Sanremo, Imperia, and Alassio — the same mild winters, the same Vermentino and pesto, at roughly half the cost. This issue maps both coasts town by town, weighs the Levante premium against the Ponente value, and shows where the inland stone villages offer Liguria's best retirement affordability.

newsletters.title: Trentino-Alto Adige
newsletters.subtitle: The Alpine Symphony
newsletters.shortDescription: Two languages, Dolomite trailheads, Swiss-grade healthcare at Italian prices.
newsletters.description: Italy's northernmost region runs on two languages, two autonomous provinces, and a quality of life that tops every national ranking. Bolzano and Trento anchor a valley network of apple orchards, cable-car commutes, and Dolomite trailheads — with healthcare that functions like Switzerland's at Italian prices. This issue maps the property rules foreigners actually face, compares eleven towns on real budgets, and explains the autonomy dividend that keeps taxes local and services exceptional.

newsletters.title: Veneto
newsletters.subtitle: The European Crossroads
newsletters.shortDescription: Padova's hospitals, Palladian Vicenza and Italy's best-connected rail.
newsletters.description: Beyond Venice's lagoon lies Italy's quiet powerhouse: Padova's world-class hospitals, Vicenza's Palladian elegance, Prosecco hills, Dolomite ski runs, and a rail network that puts Munich closer than Rome. This issue maps the mainland cities retirees actually live in, breaks down cost of living across a dozen towns, and explains why Veneto's infrastructure makes it Italy's most connected region.

newsletters.title: Lazio
newsletters.subtitle: Rome, the Hills, and the Lakes
newsletters.shortDescription: Beyond Rome: hill towns, volcanic lakes and a quieter Tyrrhenian coast.
newsletters.description: Lazio is far more than Rome. Beyond the GRA sit Apennine hill towns, volcanic lakes at Bracciano and Bolsena, and a Tyrrhenian coast from Sperlonga to Gaeta — where rents fall by half and the traffic stops. This issue covers what living here actually costs inside and outside the city, how central-Italy rail puts Naples and Florence within a short hop, where the thermal springs are worth your weekends, and why only a handful of Rieti-province towns qualify for the 7% flat tax.

newsletters.title: Molise
newsletters.subtitle: Italy's Quietest Frontier
newsletters.shortDescription: €40k stone houses, the 7% flat tax and the honest trade-off of depopulation.
newsletters.description: Italy's second-smallest region — and its quietest retirement frontier. From Termoli's Adriatic coast to Agnone's snowy hill towns, Molise pairs €40k stone houses and the 7% retiree flat tax with Cardarelli and Gemelli Molise healthcare, Tintilia wine, white truffles, and the honest trade-off of depopulation. A clear-eyed field guide for retirees who want the real Molise, not the postcard.

newsletters.title: Calabria
newsletters.subtitle: Where Two Seas Meet the Mountains
newsletters.shortDescription: Two coasts, the Sila highlands and 7% flat-tax towns.
newsletters.description: Italy's rugged toe, where the Tyrrhenian and Ionian coasts frame Sila and Aspromonte highlands. Tropea's cliffs, Reggio's bronzes, Arbereshe villages, and the 7% flat-tax towns that make Calabria one of Europe's most overlooked retirement frontiers.

newsletters.description: Italy's green heart between Rome and Florence: medieval hill towns, black truffles, Sagrantino wine, and affordable central Italian living without the Tuscan price tag.

newsletters.description: Northern Italy's economic powerhouse meets Alpine beauty: Milan's world-class healthcare, Lake Como's elegance, and why Lombardia offers sophisticated urban retirement with mountain access.

newsletters.description: Retiring to Italy's sun-soaked heel: affordable coastal living, trulli house ownership, healthcare access, and why Puglia offers Italy's best value for retirees seeking Mediterranean warmth.

newsletters.description: Your complete retirement blueprint for Piemonte: healthcare infrastructure, cost breakdowns for 15+ towns, property market insights, and expat community connections. Wine country living made practical.

newsletters.title: Friuli-Venezia Giulia
newsletters.subtitle: Where Empires Meet
newsletters.shortDescription: Italy's intersection of empires, from Trieste to the Karst plateau.
newsletters.description: Italy's intersection of empires, from Trieste to the Karst plateau.
newsletters.summary: Italy's north-east corner packs a Habsburg port, a wine-growing plain and the Julian Alps into one small region. This guide compares Trieste's coast, Udine's plain and the border valleys on real costs, healthcare and winters.
